Phonetics-Phonology_Interface.stress: Initial stress is default at the lexical level.
Phonetics-Phonology_Interface.vowel_harmony: Phonological vowel classes condition morphological suffix allomorphy.

Phonology-Morphology_Interface.quantity: Vowel and consonant length interact with morphology and orthography.
Phonology-Morphology_Interface.allomorphy: Morphological exponence may be conditioned by stem phonology.

Morphology-Syntax_Interface.case: Nominal suffixes encode syntactic/semantic relations while verbal morphology can encode participant information.

Syntax-Semantics_Interface.focus: Preverbal focus has a systematic interpretation as identificational/exhaustive focus in many analyses.
Syntax-Semantics_Interface.word_order: Constituent order contributes to information-structural meaning.

Semantics-Pragmatics_Interface.topic_focus: Topic and focus organize discourse reference and prosodic prominence.
Semantics-Pragmatics_Interface.definiteness: Definiteness, discourse accessibility and object structure interact in the verbal system.

patient.definition: GOLD: A semantic role, often unmarked, that typically does not act with volition, instigate an event, receive something, or experience a sensory impression. A prototypical patient undergoes a physical, visible change in state. Often the subject of a intransitive verb or the logical complement of a transitive verb. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/patient]

acousticRealization.definition: GOLD: The relation between some linguistic unit and its corresponding spoken expression. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/acousticRealization]

agrees.definition: GOLD: A relation holding between syntactic units, often manifesting itself in shared form features. NOTE: this could be better defined once syntactic roles and relations are developed. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/agrees]

allomorph.definition: GOLD: The relation that holds between a morpheme and one of its morphs, an occurrence of a morpheme in context. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/allomorph]

allophone.definition: GOLD: The relation that holds between a phoneme and one of its phones, an occurrence of a phoneme in context. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/allophone]

ancestorVariety.definition: GOLD: ancestorVariety is the predicate expressing the basic diachronic relationship between a language variety that existed some time in the past and a variety existing at a later time such that the former has evolved into the latter through regular language change. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/ancestorVariety]

argument.definition: GOLD: The syntactic entity about which something is predicated. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/argument]

circumscribes.definition: GOLD: NOTE: still lacks development. This relation holds between two form units and represents the notion of circumscription in a morphosyntactic system. That is, (circumscribes A B) means that part of A comes before B and part of A comes after B, in the linearization of the units of a language. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/circumscribes]

coda.definition: GOLD: The closing segment of a syllable. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/coda]

constituents.definition: GOLD: The relation holding between a linguistic unit and a list (rdf:Seq) of its constituents. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/constituents]

dataStructureRelation.definition: GOLD: This subsumes all structuring relations used for LinguisticDataStructures. As a naming convention to distinguish relations in data structure from other relations, all names of dataStructuringRelations begin with 'has-'. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/dataStructureRelation]

directObject.definition: GOLD: A direct object is a grammatical relation that exhibits a combination of certain independent syntactic properties, such as the following: the usual grammatical characteristics of the patient of typically transitive verbs; particular case marking; a particular clause position; the conditioning of an agreement affix on the verb; the capability of becoming the clause subject in passivization; the capability of reflexivization. The identification of the direct object relation may be further confirmed by finding significant overlap with similar direct object relations previously established in other languages. This may be done by analyzing correspondence between translation equivalents. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/directObject]

feature.definition: GOLD: The relation between a linguistic unit and a linguistic feature. A feature inheres in its host. NOTE: this relation is distinct from the hasFeature which pertains to data structures. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/feature]

follows.definition: GOLD: This relation holds between two linguistic units and represents the inverse of 'precedes'. That is, (follows A B) means that A comes after B in the linearization of the realization of linguistic signs. The inverse of this relation is 'precedes'. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/follows]

freeTranslation.definition: GOLD: The relation between an orthographic expression in one language and some orthographic expression in another such that both expressions have exactly the same meaning. The words in the translation may not correspond to those in the source expression. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/freeTranslation]

geneticallyRelated.definition: GOLD: geneticallyRelated is the basic kinship relation between languages varieties. If two language varieties are genetically related, then this implies that both varieties are derived from a common proto-language. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/geneticallyRelated]

hasComplexValue.definition: GOLD: This relates a ComplexSpecification to a FeatureStructure, thus giving a FeatureStructure its recursive properties. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasComplexValue]

hasConstituent.definition: GOLD: The relation hasConstituent is an abstract partial ordering relation that expresses dominance between two linguistic units. This relation is meant to cover all possible types of linguistic constituency: phonological, morphological, syntactic, etc. constituency. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasConstituent]

hasConstraint.definition: GOLD: This relates a FeatureSystem to a FeatureConstraint. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasConstraint]

hasFeature.definition: GOLD: This relates a FeatureSpecification to a type of LinguisticProperty. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasFeature]

hasForm.definition: GOLD: The relation that associates some LinguisticSign with its FormUnit. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasForm]

hasGlosses.definition: GOLD: The binary relation holding between an instance of interlinear glossed text (IGT) and a sequence of labels or 'grams' used to describe the morphemes of the IGT. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasGlosses]

hasGrammar.definition: GOLD: The relation that holds between a LinguisticSign and a GrammaticalUnit. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasGrammar]

hasLexicalItem.definition: GOLD: The relation between a Lexicon and its contents, instances of LexicalItem. NOTE: this could probably be replaced by the memberOf relation from set theory. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasLexicalItem]

hasLexicalUnit.definition: GOLD: This relates a LexicalItem to a LexicalUnit, those elements commonly represented in a dictionary. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasLexicalUnit]

hasMeaning.definition: GOLD: The relation that associates some LinguisticSign with a SemanticUnit. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasMeaning]

hasMorphologicalConstituent.definition: GOLD: The relation hasMorphologicalConstituent is an abstract partial ordering relation that expresses dominance between two morphological units. This relation is meant to cover all possible types of morphological constituency. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasMorphologicalConstituent]

hasProperty.definition: GOLD: The relation between a linguistic unit and a linguistic property, e.g., (m1 hasProperty AllativeCase) where m1 is an instance of Morpheme. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasProperty]

hasSourceLine.definition: GOLD: The binary relation holding between an instance of interlinear glossed text and a linguistic unit (clause, phrase, etc.) from the source language. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasSourceLine]

hasSpecification.definition: GOLD: This relates a FeatureStructure to a FeatureSpecification. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasSpecification]

hasSyntacticConstituent.definition: GOLD: The relation hasSyntacticConstituent is an abstract partial ordering relation that expresses dominance between two syntactic units. This relation is meant to cover all possible types of syntactic constituency. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasSyntacticConstituent]

hasTerm.definition: GOLD: The relation between some Termset and a Term. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasTerm]

hasTranslationLine.definition: GOLD: The binary relation holding between an instance of interlinear glossed text and a linguistic unit (clause, phrase, etc.) acting as a free translation of the source text from the IGT instance. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasTranslationLine]

hasType.definition: GOLD: This relates either a FeatureStructure or a FeatureConstraint to its type, expressed by an instance of PartOfSpeech. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/hasType]

inLanguage.definition: GOLD: The relation that holds between a LinguisticSign and a Language. The sign is said to be a member or part of that language. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/inLanguage]

infixedIn.definition: GOLD: infixedIn is the relation between a Lexical- or SublexicalUnit and a Root. The Root is realized as discontinuous, surrounding the inserted Lexical- or SublexicalUnit. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/infixedIn]

labels.definition: GOLD: This relation names or simply associates some SymbolicString with any Entity. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/labels]

lexicalRelation.definition: GOLD: This is the superclass of common lexical relations such as synonym, antonym, etc. NOTE: this needs work. Such relations really pertain to meaning and not form units. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/lexicalRelation]

literalTranslation.definition: GOLD: The relation between an orthographic expression in one language and some orthographic expression in another such that the translation is done on a word by word, or morpheme by morpheme, basis without regard for idiomatic usage. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/literalTranslation]

morphologicalRelation.definition: GOLD: A relation holding between morphological units. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/morphologicalRelation]

mutuallyIntelligible.definition: GOLD: mutuallyIntelligible is the binary, symmetric relation holding between two language varieties such that speakers of the first variety can communicate with members of the second with relative ease, and vice versa. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/mutuallyIntelligible]

names.definition: GOLD: This semiotic relation associates some OrthographicExpression with some Entity. It differs from 'labels' in that a name is usually considered part of the orthographic system, where a label is not. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/names]

nucleus.definition: GOLD: The central segment of a syllable. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/nucleus]

object.definition: GOLD: An object, traditionally defined, is either a direct object or an indirect object. An object, in some usages, is any grammatical relation other than subject. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/object]

onset.definition: GOLD: The initial segment of a syllable. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/onset]

orderingRelation.definition: GOLD: Any relation that establishes a linear ordering of linguistic units. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/orderingRelation]

parentVariety.definition: GOLD: parentVariety is the relation of direct genetic relatedness, where there are no intermediate ancestors between the ancestor and descendant. For example, Old English is the parent variety of Middle English. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/parentVariety]

precedes.definition: GOLD: This relation holds between two linguistic units and represents the notion of precedence in a language. That is, (precedes A B) means that A comes before B in the linearization of the realization of linguistic signs. This inverse of this relation is 'follows'. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/precedes]

predicate.definition: GOLD: The predicate is the relation between the Clause and a portion of a clause, excluding the subject, that expresses something about the subject. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/predicate]

prefix.definition: GOLD: The relation between a morphological unit and the lexical unit to which it is attached. The LexicalUnit is usually a Root or Stem. The inverse of prefix is suffix. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/prefix]

realization.definition: GOLD: The relation holding between a linguistic unit and its physical form, either a spoken, written or signed expression. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/realization]

rhyme.definition: GOLD: The core of a syllable, consisting of a nucleus and coda. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/rhyme]

signedRealization.definition: GOLD: The relation between some linguistic unit and its corresponding signed expression. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/signedRealization]

suffix.definition: GOLD: The relation between a morphological unit and the lexical unit to which it is attached. The LexicalUnit is usually a Root or Stem. The inverse of suffix is 'prefix'. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/suffix]

syntacticRole.definition: GOLD: A general category subsuming relations relevant at the level of the Clause, such as predicate and subject. A grammatical relation is a role of a phrase or complement clause that determines syntactic behaviors such as the following: word position in a clause; verb agreement; participation and behavior in such operations as passivization. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/syntacticRole]

translation.definition: GOLD: The relation between an orthographic expression in one language and some orthographic expression in another such that both expressions have the same or roughly the same meaning. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/translation]

writtenRealization.definition: GOLD: The relation between some linguistic unit and its corresponding written expression. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/writtenRealization]

harmonicAllomorphOf.definition: Language-specific relation: associates a suffix allomorph with the vowel-harmony class of a stem.

marksDefinitenessAgreement.definition: Language-specific relation: associates a verb form with the object/argument configuration triggering definite vs. indefinite conjugation.

occupiesFocusPosition.definition: Language-specific relation: associates a constituent with the preverbal identificational-focus position.

occupiesTopicPosition.definition: Language-specific relation: associates a constituent with a topic position in the clause.

hasHungarianOrthographicForm.definition: Language-specific relation: associates a linguistic unit with its Hungarian standard orthographic realization.

abbreviation.definition: GOLD: The abbreviated form representing a scientific term, e.g., ACC, 2, CL. [GOLD URI: http://purl.org/linguistics/gold/abbreviation]
